Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal + bundle pricing (Snowflake + Looker options)

Connor — thanks for the ping. I ran a quick normalized comparison using current Q2 consumption extrapolated to 12 months vs Snowflake's committed discount. Notes:
- Committed spend reduces our expected variable spend by ~12% after factoring in the discount, but it increases our locked-in spend by roughly $180k annually (which we can burn down via reserved credits).
- Looker bundle at the proposed seat count looks competitive on an apples-to-apples license basis, but it assumes a single-source model for reporting which may increase migration effort.
- Metabase open-source reduces licensing cost materially but will increase support/hosting and engineering maintenance costs. Rough TCO shows Metabase becomes attractive at 24+ months if we absorb 0.5 FTE infra/ops work.

Action items: I recommend we:
1) Ask Snowflake to split the paperwork into two PO line items (warehouse vs BI) to simplify accounting.
2) Get a clean SOW from Looker for migration hours; if theyre bundled it's fine but we should have clear acceptance criteria.
3) Evaluate Metabase PoC (ravi.kumar from Analytics-Consult suggested a 4-week PoC).

I can have a more detailed spreadsheet (breakouts by line item and ASC treatment) by EOD Tue.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal + bundle pricing (Snowflake + Looker options)

Quick tech note from the analytics team perspective:
- Looker (hosted) covers our governance and modeling needs well; it reduces ad-hoc SQL touches for product dashboards.
- If we keep some internal lightweight dashboards (alerts/ops) Metabase is a reasonable cheap alternative that integrates with our shared Snowflake account; the main cost is engineering time to maintain it.
- One risk: the Looker bundle assumes use of LookML and a central modeling layer. If we don't resource that team (1.0 FTE minimum), we'll have mismatch/maintenance churn.

If procurement wants to keep flexibility, propose a phased approach: 12-month commit for Snowflake compute with the Looker bundle opt-in for 3 months (trial seats) and a 4-week Metabase PoC run in parallel. That gives us data to decide at the 3-month mark.

Marissa Cole
